newsitem.title: USA: John Du Pont lawyer disputes claims in bias suit.
newsitem.headline: John Du Pont lawyer disputes claims in bias suit.

text.p: An attorney for John du Pont Thursday disputed claims in a race-discrimination suit filed this week against the multimillionaire chemicals heir and convicted killer.

The federal lawsuit, filed Wednesday, accuses du Pont of discriminating against four black wrestlers who were part of the Foxcatcher wrestling team du Pont sponsored at his 800-acre suburban Philadelphia estate.

Du Pont, 58, is confined in Norristown State Hospital after a jury found him guilty but mentally ill last month in the January 1996 murder of Olympic wrestler David Schultz. Schultz was a coach for the Foxcatcher team.
Du Pont, whose sentencing is set for April 22, has an estimated net worth of $250 million.
The athletes contend du Pont paid them smaller stipends than white athletes and did not invite them to live on his estate.
He dismissed three of them, saying he wanted to eliminate the colour black, which he associated with death, from his life, the suit said.
"We contend that Mr. du Pont's admittedly irrational conduct does not reach the level of intent to violate the law," du Pont attorney Taras Wochok said in a telephone interview.

The suit charges that du Pont's conduct violated federal civil rights and fair housing laws, and hurt their efforts to qualify for the 1996 Olympic games. Among the four plaintiffs was 1992 Olympic gold medalist Kevin Jackson.
Wochok said he had not seen the papers, but said there were two other key factors to a defence.

"First, the suit is not ripe, since there are administrative remedies that as far as I know were not even tried, not to speak of exhausted. Second, it's not at all clear that the law applies to these circumstances. These athletes were not employees," Wochok said.
Du Pont also has been sued by Schultz's widow, Nancy, in a wrongful death complaint and he and faces expected legal claims to recover the cost of his arrest and prosecution.
